headline: Mixed signals on Arsenal's Guimaraes pursuit
paragraphs: Reports on Arsenal's move for Bruno Guimaraes conflict. One BBC Gossip column said Arsenal and Newcastle had agreed a fee; a later Sky Sports live blog instead described Newcastle as merely braced for an Arsenal approach. Both are single-sourced, uncorroborated elsewhere - treat the deal as unresolved, not done. Arsenal also faced reports of Manchester United interest in defender Myles Lewis-Skelly, and manager Mikel Arteta downplayed talk linking the club to Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr, insisting only that Arsenal remain 'very ambitious'.

Elsewhere, a Sunday BBC gossip column built around Mohamed Salah's reported interest in a Trabzonspor move also touched two of the six clubs tracked here: Bayern Munich are said to be keen on Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko, and Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reportedly wants to work with Chelsea's Pedro Neto again. Neither claim is corroborated beyond that single column. Separately, Man City's preseason opener under Maresca ended in a penalty-shootout loss to Inter, per Sky Sports.

On the pitch, Arsenal's preseason form continues: a 4-1 win over Girona in Catalonia, with academy forward Max Dowman scoring and assisting and new signing Christos Tzolis marking his debut with a goal, per Sky Sports. Sky also reported Everton have agreed a fee, around £7m, to sign Arsenal's Christian Norgaard - one of the more concrete pieces of business linked to the tracked clubs, though not yet described as completed.
